**About 12.8% of Alberta children under 18 were in poverty in 2024**, the latest year available. That uses the Market Basket Measure (MBM, 2023 base), Canada's official poverty line.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0135-01, "Low income statistics by age, gender and economic family type", vector v1792632015. It was released 2026-04-29 and is based on the Canadian Income Survey.
- **Series:** Alberta; persons under 18 years; MBM (2023 base); percentage of persons in low income.
- **Data quality:** StatCan rates the 2022–2024 estimates "good".

| Year | Rate |
|---|---|
| 2020 | 4.6% (use with caution) |
| 2021 | 8.1% (use with caution) |
| 2022 | 12.0% |
| 2023 | 11.9% |
| 2024 | 12.8% |

The rate depends on the poverty line used. The table also carries other lines, such as the after-tax Low Income Measure, and I did not pull those, so they would give different figures. StatCan advises against comparing MBM rates across different base years.

I can fetch the other measures or a Canada comparison, or give you R, Python, Stata or Julia code or an Excel workbook for this series.

Workers in Alberta's provincial and territorial public administration (NAICS 912) averaged **$1,702.65 per week in 2025**. That is about $88,500 a year if you multiply by 52. The multiplication is my own calculation, not a published figure.

This is the average weekly earnings of all employees, including overtime, in current dollars before deductions. The data quality is rated "excellent".

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 14-10-0204-01, Average weekly earnings by industry, annual, vector v1742415 (Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours). The table was released 2026-03-26.

| Year | Average weekly earnings |
|---|---|
| 2021 | $1,651.51 |
| 2022 | $1,666.95 |
| 2023 | $1,703.25 |
| 2024 | $1,677.47 |
| 2025 | $1,702.65 |

- **Hourly wage:** I did not find a published average hourly wage for this specific industry in Alberta. Table 14-10-0064-01 (Labour Force Survey) has hourly wages, but it only reports public administration as a whole, across all levels of government.
- **Scope:** The figure covers provincial government administration only. Teachers and health workers are generally classed under education and health care, so they are not in it.

I can also provide R, Python or Excel code to fetch this series if you want it.

The average total income of an Alberta resident aged 15 and over was **about $66,100 in 2024**, the latest year available. That is in 2024 constant dollars and excludes people with zero income.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0239-01 (Canadian Income Survey), vector v107680657, released 2026-04-29.
- **Recent years:** $66,000 in 2022 and $66,300 in 2023. Data quality is rated "excellent".
- **What it measures:** income per person, before tax. It includes market income and government transfers.
- **Not household income:** family or household income is higher. That is a separate table, 11-10-0190-01, and I did not pull it.

I can also give the median, which is lower than the average, or break the figure down by age, gender or city.

**Alberta's median total income was $96,600 in 2024.** That is the latest year available, in 2024 constant dollars. It is before tax and after government transfers.

- **Unit:** the figure is per economic family or person not in an economic family, not a strict "household". Statistics Canada doesn't publish a household-based median in this table. It counts each family once, and each person living alone or with non-relatives once.
- **Trend:** the 2023 figure was $98,400, also in 2024 dollars. That is a real drop of about 1.8%.
- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0190-01 (Canadian Income Survey), vector v96414571, released 2026-04-29. Reference period: calendar year 2024. Data quality is rated "excellent".

For a census-based household median for 2020, I can pull the 2021 Census figure. It uses a different definition and a different year.
